classification.difficultyReason: Use constant acceleration to calculate an endpoint speed or stopping time, then select suitable axes and sketch a straight speed–time segment with the correct starting and ending values.

children.label: a
children.prompt: an aeroplane accelerating from rest at a constant rate of $5\text{ m/s}^2$ for 10 seconds.

answer.short: Straight line from $(0,0)$ to $(10,50)$, with time in seconds and speed in m/s.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Increase in speed} &= 5\times10\\&=50\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$$
Draw a straight line from $(0,0)$ to $(10,50)$ on a speed-time graph.

spec.description: Arrowed axes and a rectangular grid; the straight solution segment rises from rest to 50 m/s at 10 seconds. Axis titles sit outside the numeric ticks. Source blue grid and axes use house grey and black; the solution segment retains blue.
spec.mathematics: Speed v=5t for 0≤t≤10. Horizontal grid interval 1 s, labelled ticks 2,4,6,8,10,12; vertical grid interval 10 m/s, labelled ticks 10,20,30,40,50. Grid extends to 13 s and 60 m/s; one numeric zero at the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer editions only; no supplied solution graph in the student prompt.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A train travelling at $30\text{ m/s}$ starts to decelerate at a constant rate of $3\text{ m/s}^2$ until it stops.

answer.short: Straight line from $(0,30)$ to $(10,0)$, with time in seconds and speed in m/s.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Time to stop} &= \frac{30}{3}\\&=10\text{ s}\end{align*}$$
Draw a straight line from $(0,30)$ to $(10,0)$ on a speed-time graph.

spec.description: Arrowed axes and a rectangular grid; the straight solution segment falls from 30 m/s to rest at 10 seconds. Axis titles sit outside the numeric ticks. Source blue grid and axes use house grey and black; the solution segment retains blue.
spec.mathematics: Speed v=30−3t for 0≤t≤10. Horizontal grid interval 1 s, labelled ticks 2,4,6,8,10,12; vertical grid interval 5 m/s, labelled ticks 5,10,15,20,25,30,35. Grid extends to 13 s and 40 m/s; one numeric zero at the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer editions only; no supplied solution graph in the student prompt.
